justification: Adds a gate that runs in CI and pre-push, the repo's first GitHub Actions workflow, AND fixes the live defect that gate found. Read-only against production, but it can block every push, and the parking-rates repoint changes what a user-facing tool returns — a wrong number there is worse than no number. Locked with 25 Python tests and 24 Jest tests.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any SQL identifier in frontend-nextjs/app/api/** or services/** names a table or alias-qualified column that information_schema does not have and that is not already listed in scripts/schema_contract_baseline.json — OR a baseline entry no longer occurs, so the baseline can only shrink. Demonstrated red three ways before being accepted: (1) with no baseline it reported 18 real findings and exited 1; (2) injecting `SELECT id FROM table_that_does_not_exist` into services/ produced '1 NEW' and exit 1; (3) adding a fictitious already-fixed entry to the baseline produced 'baseline entr(ies) no longer occur' and exit 1. It also cannot pass by silence: with no reachable DATABASE_URL it exits 2, and with an unreadable baseline it exits 2. Additionally, the 8 tod/parking-rates entries were FIXED in this PR rather than shipped baselined; the ratchet then failed with 'baseline entries no longer occur' until they were deleted, which is the shrink-only rule demonstrating itself on real work. Baseline is now 10, all dead-code or deployed-but-unproven; zero LIVE entries remain. Every one of the original 18 was re-confirmed by direct information_schema query (8 tables + 7 columns checked individually, 0 contradicted) rather than trusted from the parser that had produced 34 phantoms.

pre_impl.existing_data: information_schema.tables + information_schema.columns, scoped to the connection's real search_path (public, extensions — confirmed via current_schemas(true)). 122 tables. pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup was rejected as a source after it reported 1 row for `documents` where count(*) = 335.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed a text-based SQL reader would be accurate; it was not. The first run produced 60 table findings of which 34 were phantoms — `set` from `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET`, `the` from an LLM system prompt, `for` from a log line, `regexp_replace` from a set-returning function, and CTE names defined in a different template fragment from the one that used them. Measured before trusting, then fixed: AST-based docstring exclusion for Python, a SQL-opener test, function-call and DO-UPDATE guards, and file-level CTE collection. Final state: 18 distinct findings, all 18 individually re-verified against information_schema as genuinely absent.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No existing check compares a SQL identifier to the catalog. Opened and rejected: tests/test_dcp_schema_gate.py (inspects extracted provision text, not the catalog), scripts/brief_contract_drift.py (service output keys vs typed contracts), scripts/lint_bracket_access.py and lint_brief_failsoft.py (source lints, no DB), ~20 scripts/check_*_schema.py one-off diagnostics (non-gating, one hardcoded table each), scripts/validate_zone_code_validity.py (validates stored DATA against ground truth — same three-state discipline deliberately reused, different axis). The baseline mechanism copies the convention of scripts/check_test_baselines.py and scripts/brief_field_coverage_ratchet.py; neither exposes a reusable loader.

functions.name: iter_sql_literals
functions.input: a file Path and its full source text, for either a .py or a .ts file
functions.output: yields each string literal that both contains a SQL verb and opens with a SQL keyword, with its line number
functions.if_none: the file contributes no statements at all and is silently counted as scanned but empty, which is correct for the many API routes that hold no SQL

functions.name: analyse_sql
functions.input: one SQL string plus the set of CTE names collected across the whole file
functions.output: base table references, an alias to table binding map, CTE names, alias qualified columns, and a count of statements whose bare columns were not checked
functions.if_none: an empty reference list is returned and nothing is reported for that statement, so a parse miss produces a false negative rather than a false accusation

functions.name: load_catalog
functions.input: no arguments; reads DATABASE_URL or SUPABASE_DB_URL from the environment or a discovered .env file
functions.output: the set of table names and a mapping of table name to column names, for the public and extensions schemas, all lower cased
functions.if_none: exits with code 2 rather than returning an empty catalog, because an empty catalog would mark every reference invalid and a missing catalog must never read as a pass

functions.name: load_baseline
functions.input: the repository root path and an optional baseline file path
functions.output: the parsed baseline dictionary of accepted known defects keyed by file and reference
functions.if_none: a missing file yields an empty entry list so nothing is suppressed, while an unreadable file exits 2 rather than guessing whether it suppresses nothing or everything

values: N/A — the gate reads no business values from the database, only catalog identifiers.

queries.purpose: list every table and view visible on the connection search path so a referenced table can be confirmed to exist
queries.where_clause: WHERE table_schema IN ('public','extensions') — scoped to the real search path confirmed via current_schemas(true); a read only session with statement_timeout 30s

queries.purpose: list every column of every visible table so an alias qualified column reference can be confirmed to exist
queries.where_clause: WHERE table_schema IN ('public','extensions') — same scope and same read only session; no user table is read and nothing is written

break_it.what_happens: Invoked as `python ... || SCHEMA_RESULT=$?`, which is exempt from set -e. Hook verified with `sh -n`.

break_it.scenario: The new script lands untracked because scripts/ is whitelist-ignored, so the gate exists locally and nowhere else.
break_it.what_happens: Root cause fixed: .gitignore line 402 was `scripts/`, which excludes the DIRECTORY, and git cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded — so every `!scripts/...` line below it was inert. Changed to `scripts/*` so the whitelist actually works, then both new files confirmed with `git ls-files --error-unmatch`. Blast radius checked: no other file became visible.

Changed to `scripts/*` so the whitelist actually works, then both new files confirmed with `git ls-files --error-unmatch`. Blast radius checked: no other file became visible.
break_it.repro: git ls-files --error-unmatch scripts/validate_schema_contract.py scripts/schema_contract_baseline.json   # must exit 0; a non-zero exit means the file is ignored and the gate would not ship

break_it.scenario: The parking repoint returns a visitor-parking rate as though it were the dwelling rate, so the number is wrong and nothing errors.
break_it.what_happens: `condition` is a row selector, not a footnote. Measured live: of 123 (lga, dev_type) car_parking groups, 27 have exactly one unconditioned row, 96 have none, 0 have more than one. selectParkingRate states a single rate ONLY for the 27; otherwise it returns every row with its condition and says no single rate covers the type. It never breaks a tie by ordering.
break_it.how: Logic extracted to lib/parking-rate-selection.ts and unit-tested (8 tests) instead of being inlined and untestable. A stub returning rows[0] fails the conditioned tests; a stub returning none fails the single tests.

break_it.scenario: The LGA join key is wrong, the query returns zero rows, and zero rows reads as 'this council has no parking requirement'.
break_it.what_happens: The portal supplies display names ('City of Sydney'); dcp_setback_controls is keyed by slug ('city_of_sydney'). toLgaSlug returns null rather than '' for absent input so the caller skips the tier instead of querying WHERE lga = '' and reading the empty result as an answer.
break_it.how: Mapping extracted to lib/lga-slug.ts from the copy already inside app/api/dcp/structured-controls, which now imports it — a third divergent copy is how DQ-30 happened. 11 tests including every genuine rename.

break_it.scenario: A tier crashes and the endpoint still answers, so an outage is indistinguishable from a genuine 'no parking rate applies'.
break_it.what_happens: Each tier now records into `degraded[]` on exception; every response carries it. When nothing is found AND a tier errored, the response is 503 with unavailable:true and an explicit 'this is not a finding that no rate exists'. A clean miss stays 200 with unavailable:false. The QA silent-failure scanner then flagged the new catches and was RIGHT: `degraded` was in the payload but nothing rendered it, so end-to-end the user still saw nothing. Rather than suppress the scanner, each tier was extracted behind runTier() whose catch returns an explicit { ok: false }, and TODParkingCalculator now renders a role=alert banner listing which sources could not be read.
break_it.how: All three qa-ignore: silent-failure annotations in this route were removed rather than kept — an exception is a defect, and 'no rows' already falls through without one. Not resolved by a qa-ignore: the scanner's objection was a real gap in the fix, and suppressing it would have repeated the exact pattern this PR exists to remove.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/parking-rate-selection.test.ts   # asserts return { ok: false } + degraded.push + no qa-ignore in the route

post_merge.db_reset: None. Read-only; no migration, no write.
post_merge.secrets: Requires a DATABASE_URL repository secret for the CI schema-contract job. Until it is set, that job fails (exit 2) rather than passing — deliberate. The other three CI jobs need no secrets.
post_merge.manual_verify: 1. Add the DATABASE_URL secret in repo settings. 2. Confirm the gates workflow runs on this PR and that python-tests / frontend-tests / qa-and-liability pass and schema-contract passes with 18 baselined. 3. Confirm a fork/Dependabot PR shows schema-contract as skipped, not green.
